Award/Judgment Factual Position And Pleadings
1. A Detailed Accident Report (Dar) was filed on 30.05.2022 by the Investigating Officer.

The said
Dar was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 17.02.2022 at abo
ut 08:00 PM in which Sh.Ranjeet @ Dharmendra S/o Sh. Diwan Singh (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

As per petitioner, at the relevant date mentioned above, while he was travelling in a e-rickshaw and going to Shastri Nagar from Pratap Nagar, the driver(herein respondent) of the e-rickshaw(hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") took a dangerous turn and in the said act,
the e-rickshaw turned turtle.

PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2024.12.12 16:07:04 +0530
The driver of the e-rickshaw was drunk and he could not manage his e-rickshaw and due to this, the accident occurred and he suffered grievous injuries.
The police was on the patrol and they noticed the accident and came to the spot and took him to Hindu Rao Hospital with other two injured persons.
Hindu Rao Hospital asked the police that the date of operation would be after 18 days and then, his family took him to Safdarjung hospital and there his operation took place after 18 days.

An FIR bearing no.109/2022, U/s. 279/337 IPC,
PS Gulabi Bagh has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The DAR was treated as a claim petition.
Respondent is the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle.
Respondent was directed to file his written statement.
2. Respondent has not filed his written statement despite direction.
Therefore, his right to file WS was closed vide order dated 02.04.2024.
Thereafter, due to non-appearance of respondent, he is proceeded ex-parte.

EVIDENCE 4.
The petitioner examined only himself in his evidence as PW-1 in support of his claim.
In his examination in chief, he described the occurrence of incident in line with the facts mentioned in Para no. 1 of this award.

He further stated that he incurred a lot of money on his special diet,
medical charges and attendant charges.
He stated that he remained bed ridden for about 06 months and suffered loss of income as he is a driver.
He stated that his monthly salary was about Rs.15,000/- per month at the time of accident.
He stated that the disability suffered by him has impeded his functional capacity as he face severe problems in his vocation due to disability in his lower limb.
His medical treatment record and bills Ex.PW-1/4 (colly).
Thereafter, the matter was fixed for final arguments.
ARGUMENTS AND FINDINGS 5.
Oral submissions were advanced on behalf of petitioner.

6. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings is as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 "(1) Whether the petitioner Ranjeet @ Dharmendra suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 17.02.2022 at about 08:00 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-11EA-3032 driven rashly and negligently and owned by the respondent?

OPP." 
7.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that Ranjeet @ Dharmendra (I) (Fir 109/22 ... vs Suresh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872136/
4 is required in a Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:14 +0530 criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: As already discussed above, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 in order to prove the factual averments regarding the occurrence of accident.

PW-1 has clearly and categorically stated that at the relevant date and time mentioned above, while he was travelling in a e-rickshaw and going to Shastri Nagar from Pratap Nagar, respondent took a dangerous turn and in the said act, the e-rickshaw turned turtle.
The respondent was drunk and he could not manage his e- rickshaw and due to this, the accident occurred and he suffered grievous injuries.
The police was on the patrol and they noticed the accident and came to the spot and took him to Hindu Rao Hospital with other two injured persons.

It is stated that Hindu Rao Hospital asked the police that the date of operation would be after 18 days and then, his family took him to Safdarjung PANKAJ SHARMA Date:
SHARMA 2024.12.12 16:07:17 +0530 hospital and there his operation took place after 18 days.

Petitioner claimed compensation on account of special pecuniary damage relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicine, transportation, diet, loss of earning during the period, he was injured, loss of earning during the period of treatment, loss of future earning on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, non-pecuniary damages, damages for pain suffering and trauma, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life alongwith interest.
PW-1 was not cross-
examined on behalf of Respondent.
Further, there is nothing on record which betrays any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW-1.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.

9. The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC & 3/181 & 146/196 M.V. Act in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.

The copies of FIR, Chargesheet, Site plan, Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, MLC,
Seizure Memos of R-1 also corroborate the testimony of PW1.
10.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:22 +0530 challenge the depositions being made by PW1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc., but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view Ranjeet @ Dharmendra (I) (Fir 109/22 ... vs Suresh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872136/

sentences.text: In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant date and time, at the relevant date and time mentioned above, while he was travelling in a e-rickshaw and going to Shastri Nagar from Pratap Nagar, respondent took a dangerous turn and in the said act, the e-rickshaw turned turtle.
The respondent was drunk and he could not manage his e- rickshaw and due to this, the accident occurred and he suffered grievous injuries.
The same is duly substantiated by the site plan.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of respondent in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above discussion,
this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

PANKAJ SHARMA Date:
SHARMA 2024.12.12 16:07:26 +0530 12.

In view of the MLC, disability certificate and medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

13. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his person on account of negligence and default of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondent and in favour of the petitioner.
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?"

14 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
COMPENSATION 15.

In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:29 +0530 tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable
Ranjeet
@ Dharmendra
( I) (Fir 109/22 ... vs Suresh Kumar on 12 December, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872136/
6 of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.

The "non-pecuniary"
or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance,
cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:31 +0530 if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
16.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:34 +0530 (i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 17.
The petitioner has placed on judicial file his original medical bills, which are Ex. PW-1/4(colly).
As per the said documents, petitioner has incurred expenses to the tune of Rs.2,602/-.
In the absence of any contest to the said documents (placed on record by the petitioner), the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.2,602/- under this head.

Ranjeet @ Dharmendra (I) (Fir 109/22 ... vs Suresh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872136/
7 (ii) Pain and Suffering 18.

As per medical documents, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries, resulting in 15%
permanent disability.

As per disability certificate no. 1932 dated 21.02.2024 issued by Aruna Asaf Ali Government Hospital, Delhi, petitioner is a case of 'FUC of IT # Lt hip' and was found to have sustained 15% permanent physical impairment with respect to his left lower limb which is not likely to improve.
The aforementioned certificate was issued in terms of the directions of this Tribunal vide order dated 11.09.2023.

Accordingly, the aforementioned disability certificate could be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Union of India in Writ Petition (s) (Civil ) No (s). 534/2020 date of order 16/11/2021.

sentences.text:
It is not possible to quantify PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:37 +0530 the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock,
pain and sufferings etc. which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of actual earnings 19.

The petitioner claims that he used to work as driver and was earning Rs.15,000/-
per month at the time of accident.

In the absence of any corroborative material supporting the claim of the petitioner as to his employment or his monthly earnings,
it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi at the relevant time).
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person as on 17.02.2022 in Delhi were Rs.16,064/-.

The medical documents, MLC and disability certificate reflect that the petitioner sustained a PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:40 +0530 grievous injuries.
In view of the above facts, it can be assumed that the petitioner would have been rendered unfit to resume his work for a period of six months at least after the accident.
As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.96,384/- (Rs.16,064/- X 06).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 20.
Petitioner claimed that he has become permanently disabled after the accident.
Petitioner has suffered 15% permanent physical impairment with respect to left lower limb.

Ranjeet @ Dharmendra (I) (Fir 109/22 ... vs Suresh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872136/
8
As per record, petitioner was working as driver, therefore, disability in relation to left lower limb would certainly hamper his working capacity.
In these circumstances and in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 15%.
As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned, we may look into the photocopies of petitioner's Aadhar Card; as per the same, the date of birth of petitioner is 01.01.1986.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident i.e. 17.02.2022 was 26 years.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that Ranjeet @ Dharmendra (I) (Fir 109/22 ... vs Suresh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872136/
4 is required in a Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:14 +0530 criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
9. The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC & 3/181 & 146/196 M.V. Act in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant date and time, at the relevant date and time mentioned above, while he was travelling in a e-rickshaw and going to Shastri Nagar from Pratap Nagar, respondent took a dangerous turn and in the said act, the e-rickshaw turned turtle.
The respondent was drunk and he could not manage his e- rickshaw and due to this, the accident occurred and he suffered grievous injuries.
The same is duly substantiated by the site plan.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of respondent in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion,
this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the MLC, disability certificate and medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance,
cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.12.12 16:07:31 +0530 if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.

In the absence of any corroborative material supporting the claim of the petitioner as to his employment or his monthly earnings,
it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi at the relevant time).
Petitioner claimed that he has become permanently disabled after the accident.
In these circumstances and in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 15%.
